scope: Proposition 14.4 (Limits and comparison at fixed offsets) of the manuscript “The canonical massive continuum limit of the two-dimensional O(3) model” (preprints/The-canonical-massive-continuum-limit-of-the-two-dimensional-O3-model-October-4-2026/massive-continuum-o3.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 215 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e75bfb353c2d3374), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 112. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let N → ∞ and s → s∗ with |s| ≤ R, for a fixed type P. The fields (14.9) converge jointly in law and in all joint moments for every finite list of continuous compactly supported vector tests in the plane. The analogous assertions hold for continuous periodic tests on each fixed common physical torus. The limiting laws are determined by their moments. Two such sequences satisfying (14.1) have the same limits in their specified embeddings. At every order and component choice, the plane measures (14.10) converge on continuous compact tests and in the strong topology of S′((R2)n). Denote the ordinary limiting hierarchy at offset s ∈ I by Fs, including its moment-determined joint laws. For either inclined type, the limit at offset s is Fs+d, s, s + d ∈ I, d = A+ − Ar = A− − Ar. (14.13)
